title: Categorization and Representation of Physics Problems by Experts and Novices
claim: Reports four experiments in which experts and novices categorized physics problems differently, emphasizing principles versus literal features.
limitations: Full methods were not retrieved in this pass; Colorado PDF mirror returned 502. Not evidence about agent skill taxonomy.

title: Schema Induction and Analogical Transfer
evidence_type: original empirical paper, selected experiments and discussion
locator: pp.19–28, Part II Experiments 4–6, especially Experiment 4 methods and Experiment 5 results
claim: Comparing analogs and abstracting their common relations facilitated human transfer in these experiments; a diagram alongside one story did not reliably induce the intended abstraction.
context: Laboratory story analogies and a structurally related transfer problem.
limitations: Schema-quality associations are not independently randomized causes; examples and hints were specialized; no agent evaluation. Author-lab URL timed out; original paper read through mirror.

title: Learning and Transfer: A General Role for Analogical Encoding
locator: pp.398–399 Experiment 2 methods/results; pp.401–403 Experiment 3; coding procedures
claim: In Experiment 2, comparing two negotiation cases produced more transfer than studying the cases separately; the study used random assignment and coded solutions. Experiment 3 examined a face-to-face task.
context: Undergraduate negotiation learning with structured materials.
limitations: Human short-term transfer in designed tasks; not direct evidence for model prompting, professional expertise, or long-term learning.

title: Cognitive Apprenticeship: Teaching the Craft of Reading, Writing, and Mathematics
evidence_type: original theoretical/practice synthesis, selected methods framework
locator: Report pp.15–20 and framework table; content/method/sequence sections
claim: Proposes making expert strategies observable through modeling, coaching, articulation and reflection, with scaffolding adapted to the learner.
context: Human education and cognitive skills, drawing on earlier instructional examples.
limitations: A framework with illustrative evidence, not one controlled test of all components or an agent-instruction recipe. Illinois PDF returned 403; ERIC copy accessible.

title: The Use of Worked Examples as a Substitute for Problem Solving in Learning Algebra
locator: pp.59–61 introductory material; deeper retrieval repeatedly timed out
claim: Authors report worked-example benefits concentrated in problems with the same underlying structure as the examples.
context: Human algebra learning; five experiments reported.
limitations: Did not inspect all methods/results; no broad transfer or current-model skill-effectiveness inference justified.

title: The Expertise Reversal Effect
evidence_type: original author review/theoretical synthesis, selected examples and conclusions
locator: pp.23–25 introduction and redundancy explanation; p.29 spreadsheet example and conclusions
claim: Reviews instructional effects that disappear or reverse with learner expertise; worked-example study and imagination instruction have different prerequisites in a discussed spreadsheet case.
context: Human learning and expertise-dependent instructional support.
limitations: Review, not a pooled estimate; mechanisms concern human cognition and do not establish transformer memory behavior.

title: Dilemmas in a General Theory of Planning
locator: pp.160–164, formulation, stopping, judgment, uniqueness sections
claim: Argues that social-policy problem framing and solution judgment evolve together and cannot generally be reduced to a single definitive optimization test.
context: Pluralistic public planning and consequential policy decisions.
limitations: Not an experiment; not a claim that ordinary code tasks lack correct answers or that research can never finish.

title: Guidelines for Performing Systematic Literature Reviews in Software Engineering
locator: Version/control section and contents covering search, selection, extraction, multiple publications and synthesis
claim: Provides an explicit review protocol with search, selection, extraction and synthesis stages.
limitations: Deeper section fetches timed out and alternate Chalmers mirror returned 403; this investigation does not claim conformance to a full systematic-review protocol.

title: ACM SIGSOFT Empirical Standards for Software Engineering
locator: General Standard; Benchmarking; Mixed Methods; Systematic Review sections
claim: Research quality criteria should fit the method; benchmark validity includes representative workload and appropriate measurement, while synthesis must integrate limitations and discrepancies.
context: Conducting and reviewing empirical software-engineering research.
limitations: Normative community guidance, not experimental proof that a fixed checklist improves an agent. Live document not revision-pinned.

title: The ASA's Statement on p-Values: Context, Process, and Purpose
claim: Statistical significance does not measure effect size, practical importance, or hypothesis truth; interpretation requires design, assumptions and transparent reporting.
context: Interpreting quantitative research, including skill or design experiments.
limitations: Not a replacement for study-specific statistical analysis; publisher DOI returned 403, published PDF inspected via mirror.

title: The Garden of Forking Paths
locator: pp.1–3, theoretical framework and data-contingent analysis choices
claim: Data-dependent analytical choices can create multiple-comparison problems even without deliberately testing many hypotheses.
context: Exploratory versus confirmatory interpretation of empirical results.
limitations: Methodological argument; does not make exploratory research invalid or require rigidly freezing an evolving research taxonomy.

title: Guidelines for Empirical Studies in Software Engineering Involving Large Language Models
source_family: Baltes et al. LLM study guidelines
claim: Report model and system configuration, traces, suitable baselines, measurement scope and limitations; distinguish target capability from bundled format/tool requirements.
limitations: Guidelines, not validation of this library; published online 3 November 2026 with a 2027 volume assignment. A full open-model benchmark is not automatically needed for every local skill trial.

title: Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
evidence_type: original model experiments, selected setup and results
locator: Sections 3–5; Table1; model/inference definitions; label and format manipulations
claim: In tested classification/multiple-choice settings, label-space/input-format information explained gains beyond ground-truth label mapping; setup comprises six LMs with two inference methods.
context: Older decoder-only models and classification/multiple-choice datasets.
limitations: Does not license incorrect worked examples for agent coding or writing tasks; not current-model or end-to-end skill evaluation.

title: Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them: Overcoming Few-Shot Prompt Order Sensitivity
locator: Section2, four-example SST-2 permutation setup, cross-model comparisons; subsequent experimental scope
claim: Ordering the same few-shot examples materially changed classification performance in the studied GPT-family models; successful orders did not reliably transfer between models.
context: 2022 few-shot classification, not general instruction execution.
limitations: No present-day agent effect-size inference; does not establish a universal best ordering or prove all skills are brittle.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
evidence_type: original model experiments, selected methods and analyses
locator: Sections2–5; controlled relevant-passage position, key-value retrieval, query-aware contextualization and open-domain case
claim: Relevant-information position and distractor count affected measured retrieval/QA performance; an intervention that helped synthetic key lookup did not equally help multi-document QA.
context: Named historical models and retrieval/QA tasks.
limitations: Not evidence for a universal current context-window limit or an optimal skill length. Tool-using agents and different tasks may behave differently.

title: Strong Inference
claim: No load-bearing claim derived from the inaccessible full text.
limitations: Bibliographic/search information is not substantive full-text inspection.
